context: The author's earlier papers replace the semigroup by a \emph{hemigroup}: a family of operators $\Phi_{s,t}$ from scale $s$ to scale $t$ in which two consecutive steps compose to one, $\Phi_{t,u}\Phi_{s,t} = \Phi_{s,u}$. This cascade ties the scale to no additive parameter. With continuity in scale, symmetry, positivity and covariance under every dilation, the hemigroup axioms classify the families of kernels on the line \prog{V-line v0.1}{Thm.~7.3, p.~37}, and in $\RR^d$ the isotropic ones \prog{iso v0.1}{Thm.~3.6, p.~13}. Covariance under every dilation is more than a pyramid needs, since a pyramid is looked at only at the scales $q^n$. This paper keeps the cascade, continuity, positivity and nondegeneracy, requires symmetry or rotation invariance where a result needs it, and requires covariance at the one ratio $q$ only.

This paper rests on five releases of the author's earlier work, cited at the printed number and page. The line paper \progpaper{V-line v0.1} states the axioms on the line and classifies the families that satisfy them. Two companion papers were released with it. The first, its \emph{cone module} \progpaper{V-cone v0.1}, describes these families as a convex cone, with their generators and their computation on the line. The second, its \emph{selection module} \progpaper{V-selection v0.1}, treats locality and the non-creation of extrema. The isotropic paper \progpaper{iso v0.1} carries the axioms and the classification to $\RR^d$. The affine paper \progpaper{affine v0.1} supplies the frame families, which the supplement uses for the separability of the classical kernels.

The isotropic paper's \Matern{} kernel of index $\gamma$ at scale $t$ has transform $(1 + t^2|\omega|^2/2)^{-\gamma}$ \prog{iso v0.1}{Prop.~3.12(2), p.~16}, so it is the law at range $t/\sqrt2$. A law is \emph{self-decomposable} if, for every $0 < c < 1$, it is the law of $cX + Y$ with $X$ of that law and $Y$ independent of $X$ [\sscite{sato1999levy}, Def.~15.1, p.~90] (Definition~\ref{def:self-decomposable}). Shrinking the law by any factor and adding independent noise gives it back. These laws are the kernels of scale-space theory. On the line the kernels of the fully covariant families are exactly the symmetric self-decomposable laws \prog{V-line v0.1}{Thm.~7.3, p.~37}. In $\RR^d$, with rotation invariance, they are exactly the rotation-invariant self-decomposable laws \prog{iso v0.1}{Thm.~3.6, p.~13}, whose exponents are the $F(|\cdot|)$ with $F \in \mathcal{A}_d$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:cited-A35}(2)).

The stratum needs an argument of its own. In the continuum, for steps with a rational transform, \prog{V-cone v0.1}{Prop.~7.5(2), p.~65} (Theorem~\ref{thm:cited-A20}) decides whether the covariant interpolant of the step is admissible, the exponent of a fully covariant family. Its criterion is a condition on the \Levy{} profile: the sum of the dilates of the profile must have a nonincreasing version. The \Levy{} measure of a lattice mask is atomic, so it has no profile, and this criterion does not apply to it. Clause (3) of the next proposition settles the question on the lattice instead. Throughout, $h > 0$ is the grid spacing and $\vartheta = h\omega$ the grid frequency.

The sampled Laplace mask has an exact pyramid (Proposition~\ref{prop:grid-pyramids-infinitely-divisible}(4)). This subsection asks how it is applied on a grid, and how what it computes compares with the continuum \Matern{} family. On the line that family is computed by forward and backward first-order sections \prog{V-cone v0.1}{Prop.~7.2, p.~60} (Theorem~\ref{thm:cited-A19}). On a grid each section becomes a recursion with one state. The answers use senses (i) and (ii) of \emph{exact} and the phrase \emph{exact cascade on the grid}, as listed in Section~\ref{subsec:grid-pyramids-line}.

\paragraph{Relation to the continuum theory.} Two statements used in this section have continuum counterparts in the cone module \progpaper{V-cone v0.1}. They are Lindeberg's generator, from the supplement, and the criterion for masks.

\emph{The generator.} The Cin ray of step $\tau$ \prog{V-cone v0.1}{Lemma~3.1(1), p.~13}, the fully covariant family with the exponent $\Cin(\tau\omega)$, has at the scale $t$ the generator $t^{-1}\delta^2_{t\tau}$, one symmetric second difference (Theorem~\ref{thm:cited-A13}). Its step grows with the scale. Lindeberg's generator (Proposition~\ref{prop:lindeberg-stratum-one}) is the same second difference, held at the fixed step $h$.

The pyramid also has a twin in time, through the \emph{subordination bridge} of \prog{V-cone v0.1}{\S 4}. The bridge substitutes $\sigma = r^2/2$. It reads a function of the frequency $r$ as a function of the Laplace variable $\sigma$ of a subordinator, an increasing \Levy{} process used as a random clock. Then $F_q(r) = \sum_{i \ge 1}\log(1 + 2c^2q^{-2i}\sigma)$. This is the exponent, in the Laplace variable $\sigma$, of Lindeberg's time-causal limit kernel with ratio $q^2$ and constant $2c^2$, a cascade of first-order integrators in time. Lindeberg defines that kernel by an infinite product of first-order factors [\sscite{lindeberg2016time}, Sect.~5, (38), p.~62] and realizes it by recursive first-order filters [\sscite{lindeberg2016time}, Sect.~6.2, p.~64]. The ratio and the constant are this paper's reading of his product.
